items.title: Counting and skip counting
items.altText: A counting scene showing skip counting by 2s, 5s, or 10s up to 1000.
items.caption: Use number names and counting sequences to find “how many?”

items.title: Number chart neighbours
items.altText: A number chart highlighting a chosen number and the numbers around it (above, below, left, right).
items.caption: Identify numbers in different positions around a given number on a number chart.

items.title: Non-standard measurement by counting
items.altText: Measuring length or volume using non-standard units like handspans, sticks, cups, or bottles.
items.caption: Use number names and non-standard units to count “how long?” or “how much?”

items.title: Place value: tens and ones
items.altText: Bundles of tens and single ones showing place value for a two-digit or three-digit number.
items.caption: Demonstrate conceptual understanding of place value using tens and ones.

items.title: Equivalent representations
items.altText: A number represented in different but equal ways (decomposition, near multiples, comparisons).
items.caption: Represent number quantities up to 1000 in equivalent ways focusing on place value and equality.

items.title: Compare and order numbers
items.altText: Two or more numbers compared with symbols >, <, and = and arranged in order.
items.caption: Use place value to compare and order whole numbers using comparative language and symbols.

items.title: Add and subtract within 100
items.altText: An addition/subtraction example within 100 using objects or number sentences.
items.caption: Use conceptual understanding of addition and subtraction to add and subtract numbers to 100.

items.title: Equal and not equal
items.altText: Two sets or number sentences showing equality (=) and inequality (≠).
items.caption: Use the concept of “equal to” and “not equal to” in addition and subtraction problems.

items.title: Mental math to 19
items.altText: Quick mental strategies like doubles, making 10, counting up, and related subtraction facts.
items.caption: Use mental strategies for basic addition facts to 19 and related subtraction facts.

items.title: Conventional strategy
items.altText: A standard written method or structured frame for addition/subtraction within 100.
items.caption: Use conventional strategies to add and subtract within 100 (with/without regrouping).

items.title: Personal strategies
items.altText: Flexible strategies like friendly jumps, compensation, splitting, and constant difference.
items.caption: Use personal strategies to add and subtract within 100.

items.title: Word problems
items.altText: A real-life addition/subtraction word problem scenario with quantities and a question.
items.caption: Solve one-step and multi-step word problems within 100 using a variety of strategies.

items.title: Halves and quarters
items.altText: A whole object partitioned into 2 equal parts and 4 equal parts showing one-half and one-quarter.
items.caption: Understand one-half and one-quarter as 1 part of 2 or 4 equal parts.

items.title: Counting halves and quarters
items.altText: Multiple halves or quarters shown and counted using fraction language (two-fourths, three-fourths).
items.caption: Count in halves and quarters using concrete or pictorial representations.

items.title: How many halves/quarters make a whole
items.altText: A whole compared with halves and quarters showing relationships (2 halves = 1 whole, 4 quarters = 1 whole).
items.caption: Determine the number of halves and quarters in a whole.

items.title: Ghana money
items.altText: Ghanaian coins and notes (₵1, ₵2, ₵5, ₵10, ₵20, ₵50) arranged for counting total value.
items.caption: Recognise Ghanaian coins and notes and find the value of collections up to at least 50 cedis.

items.title: Increasing and decreasing patterns
items.altText: Number patterns increasing or decreasing by 2, 5, or 10 with missing terms to extend.
items.caption: Demonstrate understanding of increasing and decreasing number patterns.

items.title: Pattern rules and arrays
items.altText: Simple patterns showing repeated addition/subtraction, skip counting, and arrays of objects.
items.caption: Identify, create, and describe rules for simple number patterns using skip counting and arrays.

items.title: 3D objects and features
items.altText: 3D objects (sphere, cylinder, cone, pyramid, cube) labeled with faces, edges, and vertices.
items.caption: Identify common features of 3D objects of different orientations and sizes.

items.title: 2D shapes and features
items.altText: 2D shapes (square, triangle, rectangle, circle, pentagon, hexagon) with sides and vertices highlighted.
items.caption: Identify common features of 2D shapes of different orientations and sizes.

items.title: Create shapes from attributes
items.altText: Drawing 2D shapes based on given number of sides and vertices, and identifying faces of 3D objects.
items.caption: Create two-dimensional shapes based on given attributes such as sides and vertices.

items.title: Length does not change with direction
items.altText: Equal-length sticks shown in different orientations, then aligned to prove equal length.
items.caption: Prove that placement or direction of an object does not change its length.

items.title: Measuring with non-standard units
items.altText: Measuring objects using paper clips, hand spans, pencil lengths, or other non-standard units.
items.caption: Measure length, capacity, or mass directly/indirectly using non-standard units.

items.title: Compare three or more items
items.altText: Three objects compared by length, mass, or capacity using words like longest, shortest, heaviest.
items.caption: Develop understanding of measuring as comparing three or more items.

items.title: Need for standard units
items.altText: Different learners measure the same height with hand spans and get different results, showing need for standard units.
items.caption: Recognize the need for standard units of measurement of length.

items.title: Calendar: days and months
items.altText: A calendar page highlighting days of the week and months, showing before/after relationships.
items.caption: Read the calendar and solve problems involving days in a week and months in a year.

items.title: Time using hour and arbitrary units
items.altText: A clock showing hours and examples of timing events using claps or other arbitrary timers.
items.caption: Use arbitrary units and the hour on a clock to measure time for simple events.

items.title: Collect and organize data
items.altText: A simple tally chart or checklist collecting class data such as favourite food or colour.
items.caption: Use tallies, checkmarks, charts, lists, or objects to collect and organize data.

items.title: Pictographs and concrete graphs
items.altText: A pictograph or concrete graph using one-to-many or one-to-one correspondence to show categories.
items.caption: Draw and interpret concrete graphs and pictographs.
